Emily / Laura / Marissa — did a quick back-of-envelope and a short sim using the traffic CSV. Notes and assumptions below (happy to expand to a worksheet):

Assumptions
- Model variant: rwd-medium-1 (quantized serving profile)
- Avg tokens/request now: 350 -> projected 520 in Q4
- Avg token generation per QPS: we assume 1.1x (inference + control tokens)
- GPU profile: A100-40GB equivalent; sustained throughput per GPU (with current runtime optimizations): ~95–110 effective QPS at 350 tokens; ~55–70 QPS at 520 tokens (varies with batching).

Simulation summary
- Current baseline (120 QPS): 2 GPUs (headroom 1.3x)
- Mid-term (Q3 peak 260 QPS): 4 GPUs (sustained) + 1 burst node (pre-warmed); supports KV cache + reduces token tails
- Target (Q4 projected 420 QPS, tokens ~520): 7 GPUs reserved + 2 burst GPUs (for telehealth windows x1.5 concurrency)

Recommended renewal configuration (staged rollout)
1) Term start (Apr 1): Reserve 4 GPUs in a dedicated pool. Configure autoscale policy to allow +2 burst GPUs for scheduled telehealth windows.
2) 90-day review: if QPS > 220 sustained, move to 6 GPUs reserved and increase burst to +3.
3) By Oct 1 (Q4 preparedness): convert to 7 GPUs reserved.

Performance safety margins
- We recommend keeping at least 20% headroom on sustained throughput to protect the 99th percentile latency SLOs.
- Enable prefix/KV caching for common clinical prompts — reduces per-GPU token load ~18–25% depending on hit-rate.

Operational asks for OliveHealth
- Share typical window schedule for telehealth peaks (time zones).
- Provide a list of the top 50 prompt families for caching work.

I'll generate a short worksheet with exact QPS->GPU math and cost delta for 4/6/7 GPU options.

—Karthik
Staff Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
